name: Adelaide Whitcomb
biography: Adelaide runs Whitcomb Ranch and rebuilt it when the family had more reputation than cash. She's generous at dinner and tough in business. She loves Hazel, though she often tries to manage her daughter's choices.

name: Agnes Reed
biography: Agnes owns the Boatmen's Boardinghouse and knows which late payer needs patience and which employer is passing the bill to her. She's warm with her boarders but wishes someone would invite her to dinner for a change.

name: Alma Baptiste
biography: Alma cooks for Calder's Run's late workers and makes better food than her bosses expect. She's thinking about a partnership, but only if she gets a real say in the kitchen she helps keep open.

name: August Renn
biography: August keeps the cemetery and assists the undertaker. He's good with grieving families, but he'd rather be asked about his books, garden, or the joke Nell told him yesterday.

name: Beatrice Bell
biography: Beatrice bakes at Hearthstone and knows a big order can lose money as easily as make it. She's reserved with strangers, close to Daisy and her uncle Jonah, and protective of her rare afternoons off.

name: Benjamin “Ben” Crowell
biography: Ben checks mine weights and keeps records for his crew. He remembers what the old collapse cost his family, and a new wage discrepancy is making it hard to stay quiet.

name: Bess Kincaid
biography: Bess performs and works at the Red Sash, where she sets her own appointments and keeps her earnings. She wants the women who live there to have a say in house decisions and hopes to put on a comedy night.

name: Caleb Pike
biography: Caleb builds and repairs boats on his father's river. He sees the new bridge as a chance to try something different, though he and Samuel argue before either hears the other's idea.

name: Clara Chen
biography: Clara opened a photography studio with her savings and a loan from her family. Paid portraits keep it running; the pictures she really wants are of workers when they're off the clock.

name: Cole Hensley
biography: Cole joined a bandit crew after losing his railroad job. He thought their latest theft hit an investor, then learned they had taken workers' pay. He wants out, but the people he frightened have no reason to trust him yet.

name: Cora Dunleavy
biography: Cora calls dances in Calder's Run and knows how to keep a crowded hall moving. She wants a fair share of the receipts and a chance to perform elsewhere without being called disloyal.

name: Daisy Cartwright
biography: Daisy works at the dairy cooperative and gets tired of hearing how easy fresh cream must be. She keeps notes on her experiments because she wants people to ask for something she made by name.

name: Daniel Chen
biography: Daniel runs the telegraph desk at the railhead and takes care with messages people would rather keep private. He's proud of his sister Clara's studio, loves a dry joke, and could use an evening when nobody needs him.

name: Dr. Lucía Salcedo
biography: Lucía runs Calder's Run's clinic and knows most families by name. She's great at seeing what a patient needs, less good at leaving her own work behind for supper or a game of cards.

name: Edith Kovač
biography: Edith keeps the baths' books in order and knows exactly what the staff are owed. People mistake her calm voice for agreement. She likes fine clothes and buildings with good lines.

name: Eliza Morrow
biography: Eliza teaches children by day and adults some evenings at the schoolhouse. She won't make a grown student feel foolish for asking a question, and she's learning to say no when the town expects her to take on everything.

name: Esther Wynn
biography: Esther copies records at the courthouse and makes sure promises are written down clearly. She's less stern than she looks: she loves word games, comic theater, and letters from her family.

name: Evelyn “Eve” Mercer
biography: Eve runs the old relay and carries select deliveries herself. She loves the freedom of the road, but she'd like a place where staying feels like her choice.

name: Felix Avery
biography: Felix deals at the Argosy and owns a small stake in the cardroom. He's charming company until a personal debt makes a customer think they can tell him how to run a game.

name: Florence “Flora” Vale
biography: Flora works the orchard and has grown a hardy graft a big buyer wants all to itself. She could use the money, but she'd rather see small growers get a chance to plant it too.

name: Gabriel Soto
biography: Gabriel repairs what other people have written off and does the job properly even when the customer can't tell. He needs a bigger workshop, but moving toward the railhead could leave his old customers behind.

name: Hazel Whitcomb
biography: Hazel is opening her own supply counter at the railhead. Her mother's loan made it possible, but it also gives Adelaide a say in the business. Hazel wants to prove she can run it herself.

name: Inés Salcedo
biography: Inés runs a produce stall and remembers what her customers like. She's organizing other sellers too, though she'd prefer her aunt Lucía stop treating every new idea as something she needs help with.

name: Iris Keene
biography: Iris owns Calder's Run's press and wants to publish a paper people can trust. She likes being invited into town life, which makes it hard when the next honest story may upset a friend.

name: Isaac Booker
biography: Isaac keeps auction records and can spot trouble in an animal that looks fine in the ring. He wants a small holding of his own and credit for the work he already does.

name: June Dempsey
biography: June works the livery and takes express rides when she needs the money. She's funny and capable with animals, but she has a habit of taking on every problem alone.

name: Kit Calloway
biography: Kit works a small claim outside Calder's Run. She knows enough to spot a promising find and enough to worry she wants it too badly. Camp life suits her, except for the lonely evenings.

name: Lena Velarde
biography: Lena guides people along the river using routes she learned through work and family. She likes choosing her own jobs, but a proposed leisure concession could close paths everyone now shares.

name: Lottie Fenwick
biography: Lottie knows what Calder's Run will buy before her shop's owner does. She wants a store of her own, keeps improving her books, and can't wait for the people who dismissed her to become customers.

name: Mabel Arnett
biography: Mabel owns Marigold House and keeps its pay, privacy, and rules clear. Her civic seat gives her a voice in town, though it also puts every business decision under a lamp.

name: Marisol Duarte
biography: Marisol runs a trading counter and brokers freight for people the larger merchants overlook. She's good company and careful with credit, especially when a customer is also a friend.

name: Marshal Elias Reddick
biography: Elias is Calder's Run's patient, well-liked marshal. A few unofficial deals he once thought were fair are now being used by people who want more. He'd rather fix furniture than explain the badge at supper.

name: Mateo Varela
biography: Mateo keeps the water records and helps neighboring households settle disputes. He sometimes makes a small exception to help someone through a hard week; now several of those exceptions need explaining.

name: Nathaniel “Nate” Brooks
biography: Nate works dispatch at the railhead and knows how one late connection can spoil a whole day's work. He's friendly, good with records, and tired of apologizing for a timetable he knows can't be met.

name: Nell Hewitt
biography: Nell apprentices at the dispensary and catches stock mistakes other people miss. She's quiet, not timid, and wants her concerns heard without everyone treating her like a child.

name: Pearl Merritt
biography: Pearl runs a small salon and chooses her own clients. She's poised at work and less sure how to invite someone into time that's simply hers. She likes poetry and doesn't need it to justify her job.

name: Rafael Ortiz
biography: Rafael works the hotel's evening desk and remembers what makes guests comfortable. He's saving to start a business of his own, even while he gives away more help than he can always afford.

name: Reverend Jonah Bell
biography: Jonah runs a church relief hall open to anyone who needs it. A donor has offered supplies with conditions that could shut people out, and Jonah has to decide what his welcome is worth.

name: Rosalie Quinn
biography: Rosalie sings at the Bellflower and helps run its local troupe. A touring company has offered her a place. She loves the people here, but she isn't ready to give up the stage beyond town.

name: Ruth Freeman
biography: Ruth keeps the washhouse cooperative's books and knows clear records help workers argue for fair pay. She's warm, funny, and would love a night with friends that doesn't turn into another meeting.

name: Sabine Roche
biography: Sabine works at the Red Sash and handles shared accounts for the women there. She wants them to buy the building if the numbers work, but she won't let anyone risk their savings on a promise.

name: Sadie Rusk
biography: Sadie drives routes and keeps the coach stop running. A railway contract could secure the station, but it might shut out the independent carriers who helped build it.

name: Samuel Pike
biography: Samuel runs the ferry and knows when the river is too dangerous to cross. The new bridge threatens his work; his son Caleb's ideas might help, if Samuel can listen before arguing.

name: Silas Quade
biography: Silas leads a small bandit crew out of Crowcut Hollow. He can be generous to his people, but he hid the fact that their latest haul included workers' wages. He still talks about going straight someday.

name: Tess Corbett
biography: Tess surveys the new rail bridge and has a design of her own that could solve a stubborn problem. She trusts measurements more than sales talk and knows ambition can make criticism harder to hear.

name: Thomas “Tom” Archer
biography: Tom helps build the bridge and sketches buildings in his spare time. He's proud of the crew's work, but a shaky platform has taught him that pride is no reason to stay quiet.

name: Vera Sutter
biography: Vera runs an independent assay office for miners who need a straight answer. Her tests are careful, even when a friend has already started celebrating a find.

name: Victor Halden
biography: Victor makes rail and land deals sound simple to investors. He believes the work can help Calder's Run, but he's very good at making sure his side gets paid first.

name: Virginia “Gin” Maddox
biography: Gin runs the Copper Mare with good food, fair pay, and music worth staying for. She wants to buy it outright so someone else can't undo years of work with one signature.
